docs.title: How to Add New A/B Tests - Step-by-Step Guide
docs.text: This guide walks you through adding new experiments using the Statsig experimentation system.

docs.title: Overview: The 5-Step Process
docs.text:
1. Create Experiment in Statsig Console
   ↓
2. Configure in experiments.config.js
   ↓
3. Prepare DOM Elements
   ↓
4. Test Locally
   ↓
5. Deploy & Monitor

docs.title: Step 1: Create Experiment in Statsig Console
1.1 Log into Statsig
docs.text: Go to https://console.statsig.com and log into your project.

docs.title: 1.2 Create New Experiment
docs.text:
Navigate: Experiments → Create New Experiment

Settings: - Name: Use descriptive, snake_case naming (e.g., blog_hero_cta_text) - Type: Select "Experiment" (not "Feature Flag") - Allocation: Start with 50/50 split between variants

docs.title: 1.3 Define Parameters
docs.text:
Parameters are the values that change between variants.

Example: Text Change Experiment 

Parameter Name: button_label
Type: String

Variants:
  - Control: "Read the Tutorial"
  - Treatment: "Start Learning Now"

Example: Layout Experiment 

Parameter Name: layout_style
Type: String

Variants:
  - Control: "grid"
  - Treatment: "list"

Example: Number Experiment 

Parameter Name: posts_per_page
Type: Number

Variants:
  - Control: 5
  - Treatment_A: 10
  - Treatment_B: 3

docs.title: 1.4 Set Success Metrics
docs.text: Define what success looks like: - Primary: Click-through rate, conversion rate, etc. - Secondary: Time on page, scroll depth, bounce rate

docs.title: 1.5 Start Experiment
docs.text: Keep it at 0% allocation initially. You'll ramp up after testing.

docs.title: 2.1 Identify Experiment Category
docs.text: Choose the appropriate category: - cta - Call-to-action buttons and conversion elements - navigation - Navigation bars, menus, tabs - blog - Blog-specific layouts and features - visual - Colors, themes, visual styling - content - Content display and organization

docs.title: 2.2 Add to Config Template
docs.text:
Edit: projects/blog/docs/js/statsig/config/experiments.config.template.js

experiments: {
  cta: {
    // Existing experiments...

    // NEW EXPERIMENT
    hero_cta_style: {
      selector: "#hero-cta-btn",           // CSS selector for target element
      experiment: "blog_hero_cta_style",   // Statsig experiment name
      param: "button_style",               // Parameter name from Statsig
      type: "class",                       // Type of change (see types below)
      className: "md-button--primary",     // For type: "class"
      category: "conversion",              // Category for analytics
      pages: ["index.html"],               // Pages where this runs
      priority: "critical"                 // Priority level
    }
  }
}

docs.title: Required Fields
docs.text: Field Description Example selector CSS selector for target element "#hero-cta" experiment Statsig experiment name "blog_hero_cta_text" param Parameter name from Statsig "button_label" type Type of DOM manipulation "text" category Analytics category "conversion" pages Pages where experiment runs ["index.html"] or ["*"] priority Importance level "critical"

docs.title: Experiment Types
docs.text:
1. Text Changes (type: "text") 

{
  selector: "#hero-heading",
  experiment: "blog_hero_heading_text",
  param: "heading_text",
  type: "text",
  category: "conversion",
  pages: ["index.html"],
  priority: "high"
}

2. CSS Class Changes (type: "class") 

{
  selector: "body",
  experiment: "blog_sticky_nav",
  param: "enabled",
  type: "class",
  className: "md-tabs--sticky",  // Class to add if param is truthy
  category: "navigation",
  pages: ["*"],
  priority: "medium"
}

3. Attribute Changes (type: "attr") 

{
  selector: "[data-exp='pagination']",
  experiment: "blog_pagination_count",
  param: "count",
  type: "attr",
  attr: "data-pagination-count",  // Attribute to set
  category: "blog-layout",
  pages: ["blog/index.html"],
  priority: "low"
}

4. HTML Changes (type: "html") 

{
  selector: ".blog-sidebar",
  experiment: "blog_sidebar_content",
  param: "html_content",
  type: "html",
  category: "content",
  pages: ["blog/*.html"],
  priority: "medium"
}

5. Style Changes (type: "style") 

{
  selector: ".blog-card",
  experiment: "blog_card_layout",
  param: "layout_style",
  type: "style",
  styleProperty: "display",  // CSS property to change
  category: "visual",
  pages: ["blog/index.html"],
  priority: "low"
}

docs.title: Optional Fields
docs.text: Field Description Example fallback Default value if Statsig fails "Click Here" className Class to add (for type: "class") "md-button--primary" attr Attribute name (for type: "attr") "data-count" styleProperty CSS property (for type: "style") "background-color"

docs.title: 2.4 Update Production Config
docs.text:
In your GitHub Secrets, update EXPERIMENT_CONFIG_JSON_BLOG_PROD to include the new experiment.

Format (JSON): 

{
  "experiments": {
    "cta": {
      "hero_cta_style": {
        "selector": "#hero-cta-btn",
        "experiment": "blog_hero_cta_style",
        "param": "button_style",
        "type": "class",
        "className": "md-button--primary",
        "category": "conversion",
        "pages": ["index.html"],
        "priority": "critical"
      }
    }
  }
}

docs.title: 3.1 Add Target Element
docs.text:
Make sure your HTML has an element matching the selector.

Example: Text Experiment 

<!-- Add unique ID for targeting -->
<a href="/tutorial" id="hero-cta-btn" class="md-button" data-hidden>
  Read the Tutorial
</a>

docs.title: 3.2 Add Anti-Flicker Attribute
docs.text:
Critical: Add data-hidden to prevent content flash before variant loads.

<div id="experiment-target" data-hidden>
  Default content here
</div>

The CSS will hide this until the experiment loads: 

[data-hidden] {
  visibility: hidden !important;
}

docs.title: 3.3 Add Tracking Attributes (Optional)
docs.text:
For custom click tracking: 

<button id="hero-cta" data-track="custom_event_name" data-exp-key="hero_cta_text">
  Click Me
</button>

Attributes: - data-track - Custom event name for tracking - data-exp-key - Links click to experiment for experiment_interaction events

docs.title: 3.4 Page-Specific Experiments
docs.text:
Use the pages array to control where experiments run:

// Run only on homepage
pages: ["index.html"]

// Run on all blog posts
pages: ["blog/*.html"]

// Run everywhere
pages: ["*"]

// Run on specific pages
pages: ["index.html", "about.html", "blog/tutorial-1.html"]

docs.title: 4.1 Enable Debug Logging
docs.text:
In your local experiments.config.js:

client: {
  options: {
    loggingLevel: "debug"  // Enable verbose logging
  }
}

docs.title: 4.2 Start Local Server
docs.text:
cd projects/blog
source ../../.venv/bin/activate
mkdocs serve

docs.title: 4.3 Test in Browser
docs.text:
1. Open: http://127.0.0.1:8000/
  2. Open DevTools: Press F12 → Console tab

Expected Console Output: 

[Statsig] Config loaded: {...}
[Statsig] Client initialized
[Statsig Renderer] Pre-hiding experiment elements
[Statsig Renderer] Applied experiment: hero_cta_text = "Start Learning Now"
[Statsig ExposureLogger] Logged exposure: blog_hero_cta_text = "Start Learning Now"
[Statsig EventLogger] Logged event: experiment_exposure

docs.title: 4.4 Test Both Variants
docs.text:
Option 1: URL Override 

http://127.0.0.1:8000/?exp_blog_hero_cta_text=control
http://127.0.0.1:8000/?exp_blog_hero_cta_text=treatment

Option 2: Force in Statsig Console Go to Statsig Console → Experiments → Your Experiment → Overrides → Add your user ID

Option 3: Clear localStorage 

// In browser console
localStorage.clear();
location.reload();

docs.title: 4.5 Test Tracking Events
docs.text:
Check exposure logging: - Should see experiment_exposure event when page loads

Check click tracking: - Click the experiment element - Should see experiment_interaction event with experiment metadata

Check Network tab: - Filter by "statsig" - Should see POST requests to api.statsig.com/v1/log_event

docs.title: 4.6 Test Instant Navigation
docs.text:
1. Click an internal link
  2. Console should show: [Statsig Tracking] Page navigation detected, resetting trackers...
  3. New exposure should be logged for the new page

docs.title: 4.7 Test Anti-Flicker
docs.text:
1. Disable cache: DevTools → Network → Disable cache
  2. Slow 3G: DevTools → Network → Throttle to Slow 3G
  3. Reload page: Should NOT see default content flash before variant

If you see a flash: - Check data-hidden attribute is on element - Check CSS includes anti-flicker rule - Check element selector is correct

docs.title: 5.1 Commit Changes
docs.text:
git add projects/blog/docs/js/statsig/config/experiments.config.template.js
git add projects/blog/docs/index.md  # Or wherever you added HTML
git commit -m "feat: add hero CTA style experiment

- Add blog_hero_cta_style experiment to test button styling
- Target: #hero-cta-btn element
- Variants: primary vs secondary button style
- Expected lift: 15-20% CTR

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"

docs.title: 5.2 Update Production Config Secret
docs.text:
In GitHub: Settings → Secrets → Update EXPERIMENT_CONFIG_JSON_BLOG_PROD

Add your new experiment to the JSON.

docs.title: 5.3 Deploy to Staging (If Available)
docs.text:
git push origin develop
# Wait for GitHub Actions to deploy
# Test on staging URL

docs.title: 5.4 Deploy to Production
docs.text:
git checkout main
git merge feature_branch
git push origin main

docs.title: 5.5 Ramp Up in Statsig Console
docs.text:
1. Go to Statsig Console → Your Experiment
  2. Start with 10% allocation
  3. Monitor for 24 hours
  4. If no issues, increase to 50%
  5. Monitor until statistical significance

docs.title: 5.6 Monitor Metrics
docs.text:
Statsig Console: - Experiments → Your Experiment → Results - Check primary metric lift - Monitor secondary metrics - Watch for guardrail metrics (error rate, page load time)

Google Analytics (if enabled): - Events → Filter by statsig_experiment_exposure - Segments → Create segment by experiment variant - Compare metrics across variants

Key Metrics to Watch: - Click-through rate (primary for CTA tests) - Conversion rate - Time on page - Scroll depth - Bounce rate - Error rate (should not increase)

docs.title: 5.7 Statistical Significance
docs.text: Wait until: - Minimum sample size: Usually 1000+ users per variant - Statistical significance: p-value < 0.05 (95% confidence) - Practical significance: Lift is meaningful (e.g., >10%) - Time window: At least 1-2 weeks to account for weekday/weekend differences

docs.title: 5.8 Make Decision
docs.text:
If Treatment Wins: 1. Increase allocation to 100% in Statsig 2. Update config to make treatment the default 3. Remove experiment code (now just standard code) 4. Archive experiment in Statsig

If Control Wins or No Difference: 1. Keep control (do nothing) 2. Archive experiment in Statsig 3. Remove experiment code 4. Document learnings

docs.title: Pattern 1: Button Text Optimization
docs.text:
Goal: Find the most compelling CTA text

Setup: 

{
  selector: "#signup-cta",
  experiment: "blog_signup_cta_text",
  param: "button_text",
  type: "text",
  category: "conversion",
  pages: ["index.html"],
  priority: "critical"
}

Statsig Variants: - Control: "Sign Up" - Treatment_A: "Get Started Free" - Treatment_B: "Start Learning Now"

Success Metric: Click-through rate

docs.title: Pattern 2: Navigation Layout
docs.text:
Goal: Test sticky vs non-sticky navigation

Setup: 

{
  selector: "body",
  experiment: "blog_sticky_nav",
  param: "enabled",
  type: "class",
  className: "md-tabs--sticky",
  category: "navigation",
  pages: ["*"],
  priority: "high"
}

Statsig Variants: - Control: false (no sticky nav) - Treatment: true (sticky nav)

Success Metrics: Page views per session, time on site

docs.title: Pattern 3: Content Density
docs.text:
Goal: Find optimal number of posts per page

Setup: 

{
  selector: "[data-exp='pagination']",
  experiment: "blog_posts_per_page",
  param: "count",
  type: "attr",
  attr: "data-posts-count",
  category: "blog-layout",
  pages: ["blog/index.html"],
  priority: "medium"
}

Statsig Variants: - Control: 5 - Treatment_A: 10 - Treatment_B: 3

Success Metrics: Engagement rate, pages per session

docs.title: Pattern 4: Visual Styling
docs.text:
Goal: Test primary color variations

Setup: 

{
  selector: ":root",
  experiment: "blog_primary_color",
  param: "color_hex",
  type: "style",
  styleProperty: "--md-primary-fg-color",
  category: "visual",
  pages: ["*"],
  priority: "low"
}

Statsig Variants: - Control: "#384D48" - Treatment_A: "#2196F3" - Treatment_B: "#4CAF50"

Success Metrics: Time on page, subjective feedback

docs.title: Pattern 5: Multi-Element Test
docs.text:
Goal: Test entire page redesign

Approach: Use multiple coordinated experiments with the same allocation

experiments: {
  cta: {
    redesign_hero_cta: {
      selector: "#hero-cta",
      experiment: "blog_homepage_redesign_v2",
      param: "hero_cta_text",
      type: "text",
      // ...
    }
  },
  visual: {
    redesign_hero_style: {
      selector: ".hero-section",
      experiment: "blog_homepage_redesign_v2",
      param: "hero_style",
      type: "class",
      className: "hero--modern",
      // ...
    }
  }
}

Statsig: Use same experiment for both, different parameters

docs.title: DO ✅
docs.text:
1. Start Small
  2. Test one thing at a time

  3. Small iterations are easier to understand

  4. Define Success First

  5. Know your primary metric before starting

  6. Set a minimum detectable effect (MDE)

  7. Test for Long Enough

  8. Minimum 1-2 weeks

  9. Wait for statistical significance

  10. Monitor Guardrail Metrics

  11. Page load time
  12. Error rate

  13. Core Web Vitals

  14. Document Everything

  15. Hypothesis
  16. Expected lift
  17. Results

  18. Learnings

  19. Use Anti-Flicker

  20. Always add data-hidden to experiment elements

  21. Test with slow network to verify

  22. Test Both Variants

  23. Manually verify both control and treatment work
  24. Check on mobile and desktop

docs.title: DON'T ❌
docs.text:
1. Don't Test Too Many Things
  2. Running 10+ experiments simultaneously dilutes traffic

  3. Harder to understand interactions

  4. Don't Stop Too Early

  5. Need statistical significance

  6. Account for day-of-week effects

  7. Don't Ignore Negative Results

  8. Failed experiments teach you what doesn't work

  9. Document and move on

  10. Don't Break Existing Functionality

  11. Always test both variants thoroughly

  12. Monitor error rates

  13. Don't Forget Mobile

  14. Test on different screen sizes

  15. Mobile users may behave differently

  16. Don't Experiment on Critical Flows Without Testing

  17. Thoroughly test payment, signup, login flows
  18. Have rollback plan ready

docs.title: Issue: Experiment Not Applying
docs.text:
Check: 1. Element selector is correct: document.querySelector("#your-selector") 2. Page matches pages array in config 3. Statsig experiment is running (not paused) 4. Browser console shows experiment loaded 5. Variant value is what you expect

Debug: 

// In browser console
console.log(window.EXPERIMENT_CONFIG);
console.log(window.StatsigClient.instance);
console.log(window.StatsigClient.instance.getExperiment("your_experiment_name"));

docs.title: Issue: Content Flash (FOUC)
docs.text:
Check: 1. Element has data-hidden attribute 2. Anti-flicker CSS is loaded 3. Scripts load in correct order (renderer before bootstrap)

Fix: 

/* In extra.css */
[data-hidden] {
  visibility: hidden !important;
  opacity: 0 !important;
}

docs.title: Issue: Events Not Logging
docs.text:
Check: 1. Tracking enabled in config: enableAutoClick: true 2. Element matches tracking selectors 3. Browser console shows tracking initialized 4. Network tab shows POST to Statsig API 5. Ad blocker not blocking requests

Debug: 

// In browser console
console.log(window.StatsigTracker);
console.log(window.StatsigTracker.eventLogger);
console.log(window.StatsigTracker.clickTracker);

docs.title: Issue: Wrong Variant Assigned
docs.text:
Check: 1. User ID is stable (check localStorage) 2. Allocation percentage in Statsig Console 3. No user overrides in Statsig Console

Reset: 

// In browser console
localStorage.removeItem('statsig-user-id');
location.reload();

docs.title: Issue: Experiment Not in Results
docs.text: Check: 1. Exposures are being logged (check Statsig Events) 2. Enough time has passed (results update hourly) 3. Primary metric is configured correctly 4. Users are actually seeing both variants (check allocation)

docs.title: Sequential Testing
docs.text: Test multiple variations sequentially: 1. Test A vs B → B wins 2. Test B vs C → C wins 3. Test C vs D → C wins 4. C is the winner

docs.title: Multi-Armed Bandit
docs.text: Let Statsig automatically allocate more traffic to winning variant: - Enable "Auto-tune" in Statsig Console - System will gradually shift traffic to better performers

docs.title: Personalization
docs.text: Use Statsig targeting rules: - Show different variants based on: - Location - Device type - Time of day - User properties

docs.title: Experiment Interactions
docs.text: Be careful when running multiple experiments: - Experiments on same page may interact - Use Statsig's "Mutual Exclusion Groups" to prevent conflicts

docs.text:

docs.text:

docs.title: Design Philosophy: Cache-First, No Hiding
docs.text:
Our experiment system uses synchronous cache-first initialization. On a user's first visit, they see the default content rendered in the DOM. The Statsig SDK initializes synchronously from localStorage cache (empty on first visit), then refreshes in the background. On subsequent visits, cached experiment values are applied instantly — no delay, no flicker.

Key principle: We do NOT use data-hidden or any anti-flicker hiding. Default content is always visible. Experiments are a progressive enhancement applied from cache.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
First visit:
1. Page renders with default DOM content (visible immediately)
2. initializeSync() → empty cache → fallback to DOM defaults
3. Background: initializeAsync() → fetches from Statsig → saves to localStorage

Subsequent visits:
1. Page renders with default DOM content
2. initializeSync() → loads cached values → applies variant instantly
3. Background: initializeAsync() → refreshes cache for next visit

docs.title: Fallback Hierarchy
docs.text:
1. Cached experiment value (localStorage, populated by previous visit)
   ↓
2. DOM default content (already rendered, always visible)

No blocking, no hiding, no flicker management needed.

docs.title: Phases Completed
docs.text:
• ✅ Phase 1: Modular Architecture — Refactored monolithic sidecar-bootstrap.js into modular system
  • ✅ Phase 2: Enhanced Configuration — Structured config with CI injection via GitHub Secrets
  • ✅ Phase 3: Event Tracking — Full tracking system (exposures, clicks, scroll depth, time on page)
  • ✅ Dev Site Parity — Dev site (analyticsbymark.dev) has identical Statsig setup to blog

docs.title: Module Architecture (Both Sites)
docs.text:
js/statsig/
├── config/
│   ├── experiments.config.js           # Generated by CI from GitHub Secrets (gitignored)
│   └── experiments.config.template.js  # Local dev template
├── core/
│   ├── user.js                         # Stable user ID management (localStorage)
│   └── client.js                       # Statsig client singleton (sync + async init)
├── experiments/
│   ├── renderer.js                     # Apply variants to DOM (text, attr, class)
│   └── bootstrap.js                    # Main orchestrator, config parsing, hydration
└── tracking/
    ├── eventLogger.js                  # Core event logging (Statsig + GA4 bridge)
    ├── exposureLogger.js               # Experiment exposure tracking with dedup
    ├── clickTracker.js                 # Automatic click tracking via event delegation
    ├── engagementTracker.js            # Scroll depth + time on page
    └── init.js                         # Tracking initialization orchestrator

docs.title: Script Load Order (mkdocs.yml extra_javascript)
docs.text:
extra_javascript:
  # Statsig SDK loaded in <head> via overrides/partials/integrations/analytics.html
  - "js/statsig/config/experiments.config.js"
  - "js/statsig/core/user.js"
  - "js/statsig/core/client.js"
  - "js/statsig/experiments/renderer.js"
  - "js/statsig/experiments/bootstrap.js"
  - "js/statsig/tracking/eventLogger.js"
  - "js/statsig/tracking/exposureLogger.js"
  - "js/statsig/tracking/clickTracker.js"
  - "js/statsig/tracking/engagementTracker.js"
  - "js/statsig/tracking/init.js"

The Statsig JS Client SDK is loaded in <head> via a theme override (overrides/partials/integrations/analytics.html) with <link rel="preload"> for optimal loading.

docs.title: Sites Using This System
docs.text:
Site Config Secret Experiment Blog (analyticsbymark.blog) EXPERIMENT_CONFIG_JSON_BLOG exp_2026_02_beta on #hero-cta-dev Dev (analyticsbymark.dev) EXPERIMENT_CONFIG_JSON_DEV exp_2026_02_beta on #hero-cta-dev

Both sites share identical JS modules. Only the config (injected by CI) differs.

docs.title: Adding a New Experiment
docs.text:
No new JS files are needed. The bootstrap handles everything via config. To add an experiment:

  1. Create the experiment in Statsig console with an obfuscated name (e.g., exp_2026_03_gamma)
  2. Add a target element in your markdown/HTML with an id or CSS selector
  3. Add the experiment binding to the GitHub Secret config:
{
  "experiments": {
    "cta": {
      "exp_001": { "selector": "#hero-cta-dev", "experiment": "exp_2026_02_beta", "param": "text", "type": "text" }
    },
    "navigation": {
      "exp_002": { "selector": "body", "experiment": "exp_2026_03_gamma", "param": "enabled", "type": "class", "className": "md-tabs--sticky" }
    }
  }
}
  1. Push config update — CI writes the config, bootstrap picks it up automatically

docs.title: Binding Types
docs.text: Type What it does Required fields text Sets element.textContent selector, experiment, param attr Sets an attribute value selector, experiment, param, attr class Toggles a CSS class selector, experiment, param, className

docs.title: URL Parameter Overrides (Testing)
docs.text:
Override any experiment locally via URL params:

http://localhost:8000/?exp_2026_02_beta=Click+me+now
http://localhost:8000/?exp_2026_03_gamma=true

docs.title: Events Sent to Statsig and GA4
docs.text:
Experiments:
- experiment_exposure          # When variant applied to user
- experiment_interaction       # Click on experiment element

Engagement:
- scroll_depth                # Milestones: 25%, 50%, 75%, 100%
- time_on_page                # Thresholds: 10s, 30s, 60s, 120s
- page_view                   # Page loaded/navigated

Navigation/Interaction:
- nav_click                   # Navigation link clicked
- cta_clicked                 # CTA button clicked
- social_share_clicked        # Social media link clicked

docs.title: Tracking Configuration
docs.text:
Tracking is controlled via the config's tracking section:

{
  "tracking": {
    "enableAutoClick": true,
    "enableEngagement": true,
    "clickSelectors": ["[data-track]", ".md-button", "a.md-social__link"],
    "engagementThresholds": {

docs.title: Phase 4: Add New Experiments
docs.text:
Goal: Scale to multiple experiments across both sites

How to add experiments (config-only, no new JS):

  1. Create the experiment in the Statsig console with an obfuscated name
  2. Add a target element in markup with an id or selector
  3. Add the experiment binding to the site's GitHub Secret config
  4. Test locally by copying the template and adding the binding
  5. Test with URL parameter overrides
  6. Push — CI injects the config automatically

Priority experiments to consider:

  1. Blog Pagination Count (blog-layout)
  2. Selector: [data-exp="pagination"]
  3. Type: attr, attr: data-pagination-count
  4. Variants: 3, 5, 10 posts per page

  5. Metric: Engagement rate

  6. Navigation Sticky Tabs (navigation)

  7. Selector: body
  8. Type: class, className: md-tabs--sticky
  9. Variants: With/without sticky tabs

  10. Metric: Navigation click rate

  11. Social Share Button Style (visual)

  12. Selector: .blog-social-share
  13. Type: class, className: social-icons-only
  14. Variants: Icon only vs icon + text

  15. Metric: Share click rate

  16. Category Filter UI (blog-layout)

  17. Selector: [data-exp="category-filter"]
  18. Type: class, className: filter-dropdown
  19. Variants: Buttons vs dropdown

  20. Metric: Category navigation rate

  21. TOC Visibility (content)

  22. Selector: .md-sidebar--secondary
  23. Type: class, className: toc-auto-hide
  24. Variants: Auto-show vs auto-hide
  25. Metric: Time on page, scroll depth

Important: Users see default content until cache is populated (typically after one visit). This is by design — no hiding, no flicker management. The variant appears instantly on return visits.

Success Criteria: - Multiple experiments running simultaneously - No performance degradation - Default content always visible (no hiding) - Variant applied instantly from cache on return visits - Events tracked for all experiments

docs.title: Phase 5: Performance Optimization
docs.text:
Goal: Meet performance budgets at scale

Performance Budgets: - Bundle size: < 70KB gzipped total - Initialization time: < 500ms (client ready) - Time to interactive: < 1000ms (experiments applied from cache) - Error rate: < 0.1%

Tasks: 1. Implement performance monitoring: utils/performance.js 2. Add lazy loading for tracking modules by page type 3. Optimize config size (evaluate compression trade-offs) 4. Add performance budgets to CI/CD (fail if exceeded) 5. Load test with all experiments enabled 6. Measure and optimize initialization time

docs.title: Phase 6: Documentation & Training
docs.text:
Goal: Enable team to add experiments independently

Tasks: 1. Write internal documentation for adding experiments 2. Create architecture overview 3. Document GA4 analysis workflow 4. Create runbook for common issues

docs.title: Phase 7: Production Rollout & Monitoring
docs.text:
Goal: Deploy to production with confidence

Tasks: 1. Final staging verification (all experiments, tracking, performance) 2. Update production GitHub secrets with new config 3. Deploy to production (master → gh-pages-prod) 4. Monitor key metrics for 24 hours 5. Verify all experiments applying correctly 6. Set up alerts in Statsig console

docs.title: Principles
docs.text:
1. Default content in DOM — Always render default variant in markup
  2. Progressive enhancement — Experiments enhance, never break
  3. Fail open — On any error, default content remains visible
  4. Silent failures — Don't show error UI to users
  5. No blocking — Experiments never block page render
  6. No hiding — Never hide content waiting for experiments

docs.title: Layered Error Handling
docs.text:
Level 1: Client initialization failure - getClientSync() returns null - Bootstrap skips experiment application - Default content stays visible

Level 2: Network timeout (background refresh) - initializeAsync() fails silently - Cache retains previous values - Next visit uses stale cache (still better than defaults)

Level 3: Experiment application errors - Catch errors during DOM manipulation - Default content stays visible - Error logged for monitoring

docs.title: Risk Mitigation
docs.text:
Risks:

  1. Statsig client not loaded → getClientSync() returns null, defaults shown
  2. GA4 blocked by AdBlock → Wrap in try-catch, fail silently
  3. Performance impact → Use efficient APIs (IntersectionObserver), cache-first init
  4. Event duplication → Track event history, check before logging
  5. Instant nav breaks tracking → Subscribe to document$, reset state properly

Rollback Plan:

  1. Set tracking flags to false in config (immediate mitigation)
  2. Remove experiment bindings from config (experiments stop, defaults shown)
  3. Remove tracking scripts from mkdocs.yml if needed
  4. Site continues working normally with default content

docs.title: Testing Checklist
docs.text:
Before deploying a new experiment:

  • [ ] Experiment created in Statsig console
  • [ ] Config binding added to GitHub Secret
  • [ ] Target element exists in markup with correct selector
  • [ ] URL parameter override tested locally
  • [ ] Default content looks correct (what users see on first visit)
  • [ ] Variant applies correctly on return visit (cached)
  • [ ] Mobile viewport tested
  • [ ] Instant navigation works (variant re-applies on page switch)
  • [ ] Events tracked correctly (check console with loggingLevel: "debug")
  • [ ] GA integration verified (DebugView)
  • [ ] Staging verification complete

docs.title: Quick Start: Adding New A/B Tests
docs.text: TL;DR: 5 steps to launch a new experiment.

docs.title: 1. Create in Statsig Console (5 min)
docs.text:
https://console.statsig.com → Experiments → Create New

Name: blog_hero_cta_text
Parameter: button_label
  - Control: "Read Tutorial"
  - Treatment: "Start Now"

Allocation: 0% (we'll ramp after testing)

docs.title: 2. Add to Config (2 min)
docs.text:
File: projects/blog/docs/js/statsig/config/experiments.config.template.js

experiments: {
  cta: {
    hero_button_text: {
      selector: "#hero-cta",               // CSS selector
      experiment: "blog_hero_cta_text",    // Statsig name
      param: "button_label",               // Parameter name
      type: "text",                        // Type of change
      category: "conversion",              // Analytics category
      pages: ["index.html"],               // Where to run
      priority: "critical"                 // Priority level
    }
  }
}

Common Types: - text - Change text content - class - Add/remove CSS class - attr - Set attribute value - html - Change HTML content - style - Set CSS property

docs.title: 3. Prepare HTML (1 min)
docs.text:
<!-- Add unique ID and data-hidden -->
<a href="/tutorial" id="hero-cta" class="md-button" data-hidden>
  Read Tutorial
</a>

Critical: data-hidden prevents content flash!

docs.title: 4. Test Locally (10 min)
docs.text:
# Start server
cd projects/blog
mkdocs serve

# Open: http://127.0.0.1:8000/
# Check: DevTools → Console

Expected logs: 

[Statsig] Applied experiment: blog_hero_cta_text = "Start Now"
[Statsig ExposureLogger] Logged exposure
[Statsig EventLogger] Logged event: experiment_exposure

Test both variants: 

http://127.0.0.1:8000/?exp_blog_hero_cta_text=control
http://127.0.0.1:8000/?exp_blog_hero_cta_text=treatment

docs.title: 5. Deploy & Monitor (ongoing)
docs.text:
# Commit
git add .
git commit -m "feat: add hero CTA text experiment"
git push

# Update production secret (GitHub)
Settings → Secrets → EXPERIMENT_CONFIG_JSON_BLOG_PROD

# Ramp in Statsig Console
10% → monitor 24h → 50% → wait for significance → decide

Monitor: Statsig Console → Your Experiment → Results

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Experiment not applying? 

// Browser console
console.log(document.querySelector("#your-selector")); // Check selector

docs.title: Statsig Configuration
docs.text: This directory contains the Statsig experiment configuration.

docs.title: Files
docs.text:
• experiments.config.template.js - Template for local development (committed to git)
  • experiments.config.js - Active configuration (gitignored, generated)
  • production-config-example.json - Example of production config structure

docs.title: Local Development
docs.text:
Generate a local config from the template:

node scripts/experiments/generate-local-config.mjs

This creates experiments.config.js from the template with local development settings.

docs.title: Production
docs.text:
In production, experiments.config.js is generated by GitHub Actions from secrets: - EXPERIMENT_CONFIG_JSON_BLOG - Blog production config

The config is validated before being written to ensure it's well-formed.

docs.title: Configuration Format
docs.text:
The enhanced config format supports:

  • Metadata (_meta) - Environment, version, timestamp
  • Client config (client) - API key and options
  • Feature flags (featureFlags) - On/off toggles (Phase 3)
  • Experiments (experiments) - Organized by category (cta, navigation, blog, visual, content)
  • Tracking (tracking) - Event tracking configuration (Phase 3)

docs.title: Example Structure
docs.text:
window.EXPERIMENT_CONFIG = {
  _meta: {
    environment: "production",
    version: "1.0.0"
  },
  client: {
    apiKey: "client-xxxxx",
    options: {
      environment: { tier: "production" },
      loggingLevel: "none"
    }
  },
  experiments: {
    cta: {
      hero_button_text: {
        selector: "#hero-cta-dev",
        experiment: "abm_dev_landing_button_text",
        param: "button_label",
        type: "text",
        category: "conversion",
        pages: ["index.html"],
        priority: "critical"
      }
    }
  }
}

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
Validate a config before deployment:

node scripts/experiments/validate-config.mjs --file path/to/config.json

This checks for: - Required fields (client.apiKey, experiments) - Valid experiment structure - Type-specific requirements (attr/class bindings) - Valid priority and category values

docs.title: Obfuscation Strategy
docs.text:
When open sourcing this repo, use obfuscated experiment names to protect strategic information:

Public (in config): 

experiments: {
  cta: {
    exp_001: {
      selector: "#hero-cta-dev",
      experiment: "exp_2024_01_alpha",  // Obfuscated Statsig name
      param: "text",                     // Generic parameter name
      type: "text",
      pages: ["index.html"]
      // NO category, priority, hypothesis, expectedLift
    }
  }
}

Private (in EXPERIMENT_MAPPING.md - NOT in repo): 

### exp_001 (exp_2024_01_alpha)
- Real Name: Hero CTA Button Text Optimization
- Hypothesis: Action-oriented text increases CTR by 15-20%
- Priority: Critical
- Status: Active

docs.title: What's Hidden
docs.text: ✅ Real experiment purposes ✅ Business hypotheses ✅ Expected results ✅ Strategic priorities ✅ What metrics matter most

docs.title: What's Still Exposed
docs.text: ⚠️ Which DOM elements are tested (selectors) ⚠️ Number of active experiments ⚠️ That A/B testing is being used ⚠️ General tracking approach

docs.title: Naming Convention
docs.text:
Format: exp_YYYY_MM_greek - exp_2024_01_alpha - First experiment of Jan 2024 - exp_2024_01_beta - Second experiment of Jan 2024 - exp_2024_02_gamma - Third experiment (or first of Feb)

Greek sequence: alpha, beta, gamma, delta, epsilon, zeta, eta, theta, iota, kappa

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Use generic parameter names: text, enabled, value, count
  2. Avoid descriptive names: NOT conversion_optimized_cta_text
  3. Remove strategic metadata: No category, priority, hypothesis
  4. Keep mapping private: Track real names in EXPERIMENT_MAPPING.md (gitignored)
  5. Minimal comments: Don't explain strategy in code comments

docs.title: Before Open Sourcing
docs.text:
1. Add to .gitignore: 

    EXPERIMENT_MAPPING.md

  2. Update all GitHub Secrets to use obfuscated names

  3. Rename experiments in Statsig Console to obfuscated names

  4. Review built site for leaked information

  5. Audit comments in code for strategic details

docs.title: Event Tracking System
docs.text: Phase 3 implementation - Comprehensive event tracking for Statsig experiments and user engagement.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
tracking/
├── eventLogger.js        - Core event logging (Statsig + GA4 bridge)
├── exposureLogger.js     - Log experiment exposures
├── clickTracker.js       - Automatic click tracking
├── engagementTracker.js  - Scroll depth + time on page
└── init.js              - Tracking initialization orchestrator

docs.title: eventLogger.js (213 lines)
docs.text:
Purpose: Centralized event logging infrastructure

Key Features: - Logs to both Statsig SDK and Google Analytics 4 - Automatic metadata enrichment (page, user, viewport, timing) - Event deduplication to prevent duplicate logs - Graceful GA4 failure handling (ad blocker safe) - Debug logging support

API: 

const logger = new EventLogger(client, config);
logger.logEvent(eventName, value, metadata);

docs.title: exposureLogger.js (125 lines)
docs.text:
Purpose: Track experiment exposures

Key Features: - Logs when users see experiment variants - Prevents duplicate exposures per page - Sets GA4 user properties for segmentation - Resets on page navigation

API: 

const exposureLogger = new ExposureLogger(eventLogger, config);
exposureLogger.logExposure(experimentName, variant, metadata);

docs.title: clickTracker.js (214 lines)
docs.text:
Purpose: Automatic click tracking

Key Features: - Event delegation pattern (performance optimized) - Tracks configured selectors: [data-track], .md-button, a.md-social__link - Extracts rich metadata from clicked elements - Smart event naming based on context

API: 

const clickTracker = new ClickTracker(eventLogger, config);
clickTracker.init();

docs.title: engagementTracker.js (272 lines)
docs.text:
Purpose: Scroll depth and time on page tracking

Key Features: - Scroll depth using IntersectionObserver (25%, 50%, 75%, 100%) - Time on page using setTimeout (10s, 30s, 60s, 120s) - Respects page visibility (pauses when tab hidden) - Resets state on page navigation

API: 

const engagementTracker = new EngagementTracker(eventLogger, config);
engagementTracker.init();

docs.title: init.js (138 lines)
docs.text:
Purpose: Tracking system orchestrator

Key Features: - Reads config and initializes enabled trackers - Waits for Statsig client before starting - Subscribes to instant navigation events - Handles errors gracefully

API: 

await window.StatsigTracker.init();

docs.title: Experiment Events
docs.text:
• experiment_exposure - When variant shown to user
  • experiment_interaction - Click on experiment element

docs.title: Engagement Events
docs.text:
• scroll_depth - Milestones: 25%, 50%, 75%, 100%
  • time_on_page - Thresholds: 10s, 30s, 60s, 120s
  • page_view - Page loaded/navigated

docs.title: Interaction Events
docs.text:
• nav_click - Navigation link clicked
  • cta_clicked - CTA button clicked
  • social_share_clicked - Social media link clicked
  • click - Generic click (fallback)

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Tracking behavior is controlled by window.EXPERIMENT_CONFIG.tracking:

tracking: {
  // Enable/disable automatic click tracking
  enableAutoClick: true,

  // Enable/disable engagement tracking (scroll + time)
  enableEngagement: true,

  // Selectors for automatic click tracking
  clickSelectors: [
    "[data-track]",        // Custom tracking attribute
    ".md-button",          // Material buttons
    "a.md-social__link"    // Social share links
  ],

  // Engagement tracking thresholds
  engagementThresholds: {
    scrollDepth: [25, 50, 75, 100],    // Percentages
    timeOnPage: [10, 30, 60, 120]      // Seconds
  },

  // Google Analytics 4 integration
  googleAnalytics: {
    enabled: true,              // Send to GA4
    sendExposures: true,        // Send exposure events
    sendCustomEvents: true,     // Send custom events
    prefix: "statsig_"          // Event name prefix
  }
}

docs.text:
• [ ] Exposure logged when experiment variant applied
  • [ ] Click events logged for tracked elements

docs.title: Performance
docs.text:
Bundle Size: ~28 KB unminified (~8-10 KB gzipped)

Initialization Time: < 100ms (async, non-blocking)

Runtime Overhead: Negligible (event delegation, passive observers)

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
The tracking system is designed to fail gracefully:

  1. Statsig client unavailable → Tracking disabled, site works normally
  2. GA4 blocked → GA4 fails silently, Statsig continues
  3. Tracking init fails → Error logged, experiments still work
  4. Individual tracker fails → Other trackers continue working

All errors are logged to console but don't break the site.

docs.title: Instant Navigation Support
docs.text:
The tracking system fully supports MkDocs Material instant navigation:

  1. Page loads → Tracking initialized
  2. User clicks internal link → Navigation event fires
  3. document$ emits → Tracking system resets
  4. New content loaded → Tracking re-initializes
  5. New exposures logged → Process continues

docs.title: Integration with Bootstrap
docs.text:
The bootstrap.js file has two integration points:

1. Exposure Logging (line ~109): Called after applying experiment variant: 

if (window.StatsigTracker?.exposureLogger) {
  window.StatsigTracker.exposureLogger.logExposure(...);
}

2. Tracking Initialization (line ~160): Called after experiments initialized: 

if (window.StatsigTracker?.init) {
  window.StatsigTracker.init().catch(error => { ... });
}

docs.title: No events logged
docs.text:
• Check if tracking enabled in config
  • Verify Statsig client initialized
  • Check browser console for errors

docs.title: GA4 events not appearing
docs.text:
• Check if GA4 blocked by ad blocker (expected, OK)
  • Verify googleAnalytics.enabled: true
  • Check if gtag function exists

docs.title: Duplicate events
docs.text:
• Check deduplication logic
  • Verify page navigation resets state

docs.title: Scroll tracking not working
docs.text:
• Verify page has sufficient height
  • Check if IntersectionObserver supported
  • Inspect DOM for scroll markers
